_DESCRIPTIONS.create_sequence_database: Build a retained nucleotide or protein BLAST database from supplied FASTA sequences.
_DESCRIPTIONS.extract_sequences: Retrieve explicitly selected sequences or ranges from a supplied prepared BLAST database.
_DESCRIPTIONS.info: Read the selected prepared BLAST database’s native counts, molecule and volume information.
_DESCRIPTIONS.metadata: Retrieve the selected prepared BLAST database’s native JSON metadata and file inventory.
_DESCRIPTIONS.integrity: Run the explicitly selected BLAST database integrity checks and preserve their actual coverage and diagnostics.

_INSTRUCTIONS.create_sequence_database: Supply one plain FASTA and choose nucleotide or protein, database format4 or5, title, identifier parsing and hash-index options explicitly. Optional taxonomy maps and masking artifacts must be supplied with their own identities; selecting this job does not generate either. Keep every produced database component, including native metadata and sidecars. A zero exit does not establish that every file was captured or that a later search used the database. A failed build can leave partial files; retain them without presenting a usable prepared database. Taxonomy assignments describe the selected inputs and do not establish gene function.
_INSTRUCTIONS.extract_sequences: Select an already prepared database and an explicit list of sequence identifiers. This binding does not select a default database or retrieve all entries. Duplicate requests remain distinct. Native identifier, accession, OID and full sequence length accompany the returned sequence. A requested range uses one-based inclusive endpoints; retained normalized coordinates use zero-based half-open endpoints. The returned fragment length is distinct from the full sequence length. Preserve strand, missing identifiers and unassociated rows. Do not join records by output position or choose the first duplicate accession. get_dups and target_only are mutually exclusive native options.
_INSTRUCTIONS.info: Select the exact prepared database. Retain the native title, database format, molecule, sequence/residue counts and volume identities when reported. Select exact_length explicitly if that measurement is needed. Absent counts remain unavailable. Counts describe this database population, not the frequency of a function.
_INSTRUCTIONS.metadata: Select the exact prepared database and retain its native metadata JSON. Preserve native reported file names, byte totals, sequence counts, residue counts and original field locations. Native metadata is not itself the workflow prepared-database manifest. Writer metadata and later inspection metadata can include different file populations; do not silently substitute one byte total for another.
_INSTRUCTIONS.integrity: Select the exact prepared database and the full or sampled checking methods. Preserve the native diagnostic output and return code. Requested sampling counts do not establish actual checked counts or sampled OIDs. A sampled pass is not a full database pass. Retain useful passing sequence checks even when another check fails. Missing taxonomy data, missing files and an execution failure are distinct from evidence that sequences are corrupt. Required reference data must be explicitly configured; no lookup or download is added automatically.

suffix: Commission the selected job through launch and its configured local-compute child under the caller’s allocation. It is one native utility invocation; preparation, extraction and integrity checking are separately selected operations. The infrastructure does not choose follow-up work. Retain original inputs, output files and diagnostic streams. Results acquisition uses the deterministic typed utility records and returns only the parent’s requested fields. These are supporting operations without an independent annotation-confidence score. Keep database-scale work off this local resource; remote execution requires its own actually configured resource binding.
